questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: Before a passenger aircraft is fuelled for a long journey, the ground crew has to work out how much fuel the flight will need in total. Consider the following statements. 1. If the crew works out the fuel requirement from the density of fuel in pounds (lb) per litre rather than kilograms (kg) per litre, the aircraft can be left about 15,000 litres short of the fuel it needs. 2. Using standard (SI) units everywhere avoids conversions and errors, so measuring in pounds (lb) per litre rather than kilograms (kg) per litre makes no difference to the amount of fuel the aircraft carries. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
